def max_window_sum(xs, k):
    if k <= 0 or k > len(xs):
        return None
    
    # Initialize the first window sum
    current_sum = sum(xs[:k])
    best_sum = current_sum
    
    # Slide the window
    for i in range(k, len(xs)):
        # Add the new element and subtract the element leaving the window
        current_sum = current_sum + xs[i] - xs[i - k]
        if current_sum > best_sum:
            best_sum = current_sum
            
    return best_sum
```

def max_window_sum(xs, k):
    if k <= 0 or k > len(xs):
        return None
    
    # Initialize the first window sum
    current_sum = sum(xs[:k])
    best = current_sum
    
    # Slide the window
    # The loop runs until the last element of the array is added to the window
    for i in range(k, len(xs)):
        # To slide the window of size k, we remove xs[i-k] and add xs[i]
        # i is the index of the new element entering the window
        # i-k is the index of the element leaving the window
        current_sum = current_sum - xs[i - k] + xs[i]
        
        if current_sum > best:
            best = current_sum
            
    return best

def merge_intervals(intervals):
    merged = []
    if not intervals:
        return []
        
    sorted_intervals = sorted(intervals)
    
    current_start, current_end = sorted_intervals[0]
    
    for next_start, next_end in sorted_intervals[1:]:
        if next_start <= current_end:
            # Overlap or touch, extend the current merged interval
            current_end = max(current_end, next_end)
        else:
            # No overlap, finalize the current interval and start a new one
            merged.append([current_start, current_end])
            current_start, current_end = next_start, next_end
            
    # Add the last processed interval
    merged.append([current_start, current_end])
    
    return merged
```

def merge_intervals(intervals):
    if not intervals:
        return []

    # Sort intervals primarily by start time
    intervals.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])

    merged = []
    for current_start, current_end in intervals:
        # If the merged list is empty or the current interval starts after the end of the last merged interval
        if not merged or current_start > merged[-1][1]:
            merged.append([current_start, current_end])
        # Check for overlap or touching (current_start <= merged[-1][1])
        elif current_start <= merged[-1][1]:
            # Update the end of the last interval to be the maximum of the two ends
            merged[-1][1] = max(merged[-1][1], current_end)
            
    return merged
```

def merge_intervals(intervals):
    merged = []
    # Sort by the start time of each interval
    sorted_intervals = sorted(intervals)
    
    for current_start, current_end in sorted_intervals:
        # If merged is empty, or if the current interval starts after the last merged interval ends, add it directly
        if not merged or current_start > merged[-1][1]:
            merged.append([current_start, current_end])
        # Otherwise, there is an overlap, so merge by extending the end of the last interval
        elif current_start <= merged[-1][1]:
            merged[-1][1] = max(merged[-1][1], current_end)
            
    return merged

def paginate(items, page, per_page=10):
    if page < 1:
        return []
    start = (page - 1) * per_page
    end = start + per_page
    return items[start:end]
```
